main.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Justice for All
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Trials and Tribulations

Ace Attorney.notes: Main = Wikipedia's six main-series games, using the Japanese GBA originals (2001/2002/2004) as IGDB entries; the DS 'Phoenix Wright' versions are IGDB expanded games of these. Investigations 1-2, Layton crossover and Great Ace Attorney 1-2 are spin-offs per Wikipedia. Dropped: Project X Zone 2 (crossover), two fan games (Turnabout Substitution, Golden Witch), Gyakuten Saiban Jiten (reference app), Joypolis attraction.

Alone in the Dark.notes: Illumination (2015) is not in the IGDB cache, given by name. Ghosthunter is an unrelated Cambridge Studio game, dropped. 2024 game is a reimagining of the 1992 original.

Animal Crossing.notes: First entry uses the N64 original Doubutsu no Mori (2001); the 2002 GameCube 'Animal Crossing' (id 2655) is an IGDB expanded game of it. Happy Home Designer, Amiibo Festival and Pocket Camp are spin-offs per Wikipedia (left to the checkbox). Dropped: e-Reader/N64 minigames and the Photos/Plaza companion apps.

Assassin's Creed.notes: Liberation and Freedom Cry are spin-offs per Wikipedia (Freedom Cry started as Black Flag DLC). Discovery Tour entries are educational modes of Origins/Odyssey/Valhalla, dropped. Black Flag Resynced released 2026-07-09.

Battlefield.notes: Battlefield 1942, Hardline, Heroes and Play4Free are not in the IGDB cache (only the 1942 Complete Collection bundle 284924 is), given by name. Wikipedia's list puts 2: Modern Combat (console) and 1943 (downloadable) among the main games; kept as main though many players treat them as side entries. Hardline is a spin-off per Wikipedia.

Borderlands.notes: Matches the current output. Tales, New Tales, Wonderlands and Assault on Dragon Keep are spin-offs.

Call of Duty.notes: 23 annual main entries per Wikipedia. Both Warzone releases (131800, 217815) are free-to-play spin-offs. Modern Warfare 4 released 2026-10-23.

games.title: Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse
Castlevania Chronicles
Castlevania (Nintendo 64)

Castlevania.notes: Follows Wikipedia's main-series table, which includes Vampire Killer, Haunted Castle, Castlevania Legends and Legacy of Darkness. Castlevania III uses the Japanese original Akumajou Densetsu (151162); the US release 1119 is an IGDB port of it. Castlevania Chronicles uses the 1993 X68000 original (215375); 19468 is the 2001 PS version. Super Castlevania IV is listed as a main entry, not a remake, although IGDB types it as a remake of Castlevania. Dracula X Chronicles and Haunted Castle Revisited are remakes Wikipedia lists under compilations. Lords of Shadow is a separate reboot table on Wikipedia.

main.title: Crash Bandicoot 2: Cortex Strikes Back (N. Sane Trilogy)

Crash Bandicoot.notes: Main = Wikipedia's console platformers. GBA handheld platformers (Huge Adventure, N-Tranced, Purple) are a separate Wikipedia table; left as spin-offs. N. Sane Trilogy is one 2017 compilation of three remakes; IGDB has three remake ids. Dropped: LCD handheld and mobile titles that IGDB does not tag as mobile.

Diablo.notes: Diablo Immortal is a mobile-first MMO spin-off per Wikipedia (it also runs on PC, so the mobile filter misses it). Expansions and Diablo II: Resurrected (remaster) are not separate entries.

games.title: Donkey Kong Jr.
Donkey Kong (1994)

Donkey Kong.notes: Wikipedia groups these as arcade games, Country, Land and Mario vs. Donkey Kong tables. DK64, Jungle Beat and Bananza (3D/standalone platformers) are put in the first section, and Donkey Kong (1994, Game Boy) is kept there as a main game; Wikipedia's tables are loose here. Diddy Kong Racing, Donkey Konga, Barrel Blast, King of Swing and Jungle Climber stay as spin-offs. NES Remix is a crossover compilation, dropped.

Double Dragon.notes: Wikipedia's classic list also includes Battletoads/Double Dragon (crossover), the 1995 Neo Geo fighting game and Game Boy/Game Gear versions; kept as spin-offs since players do not count them as mainline. Neon is listed by Wikipedia under remakes/reimaginings but is a new game, so it is main without remake_of. Revive (2025) is a reboot in Wikipedia's revived series.

main.title: Dragon Quest III (Game Boy Color remake)

Dragon Quest.notes: Main = I to XI (XII unreleased). Monsters, Heroes, Builders, Torneko, Slime are spin-off series per Wikipedia. Remakes listed are the console remakes Wikipedia names; the mobile-derived ids 1812, 1813, 1814 (2004/2005/2009 'Dragon Quest', 'II: Luminaries', 'III: Seeds of Salvation') are left out of main and will show as spin-offs. 271211 is a duplicate JP entry of the DS Dragon Quest IV (1815).

Fallout.notes: Wikipedia's main series is Fallout 1 to 4 (5 unreleased) and explicitly classes New Vegas (16) and Fallout 76 (103020) as spin-offs, so they are left to the spin-off checkbox. Many players count New Vegas as mainline; promote 16 if you prefer player convention over Wikipedia.

Far Cry.notes: Wikipedia main series is the numbered games only. Blood Dragon (standalone expansion), Primal, New Dawn, Instincts, Instincts: Evolution, Vengeance and VR are spin-offs and stay behind the checkbox (all attached in IGDB). Far Cry Instincts is not a remake of Far Cry despite IGDB's remake typing.

main.title: Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn

Final Fantasy.notes: Main = numbered I to XVI; XIV appears twice as Wikipedia lists both the 2010 original and the 2013 relaunch. IGDB 426 is FF VI under its US SNES title 'Final Fantasy III'. FF VII uses 393025 (original JP release, type 0); the popular IGDB entry 427 (1641 ratings) is its 'expanded game' child, so the app may want to inherit ratings from 427. Direct sequels X-2, XIII-2, Lightning Returns and Tactics, Crisis Core, Type-0, Pocket Edition are spin-offs per Wikipedia's grouping. 2406 is a 2005 Verizon phone 'Final Fantasy VII' entry with no ratings.

main.title: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light
Fire Emblem: Mystery of the Emblem
Fire Emblem: New Mystery of the Emblem

Fire Emblem.notes: Fates Birthright and Conquest are paired versions (both listed); Revelation is typed as DLC in IGDB (18038) and omitted. Fortune's Weave released 2026-09-17. Warriors, Three Hopes, Heroes, Tokyo Mirage Sessions, Shadows, BS Fire Emblem are spin-offs (all attached in IGDB).

Five Nights at Freddy's.notes: Wikipedia counts 11 main installments, Secret of the Mimic being the eleventh; Ultimate Custom Night and Help Wanted 2 are main, Into the Pit is a spin-off. Dropped Popgoes Arcade and MyPopgoes (fan-developed Popgoes series).

God of War.notes: Wikipedia mainline = the six Santa Monica Studio entries. Chains of Olympus, Ghost of Sparta, Sons of Sparta (2026) and Betrayal are side games (attached in IGDB, so they show as spin-offs). 7390 PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale is a crossover.

Grand Theft Auto.notes: Wikipedia main titles; GTA VI (52189) releases 2026-11-19 and should be added then. Handheld games (Advance, Liberty City Stories, Vice City Stories, Chinatown Wars) are listed by Wikipedia in a separate handheld section; some players count LCS/VCS as mainline. 62701 iFruit is a companion app.

Half-Life.notes: Wikipedia main games are Half-Life, Half-Life 2 and Alyx; Episodes One and Two are Valve's direct continuations and most players count them as main, so included. Opposing Force, Blue Shift, Decay (Gearbox expansions), Black Mesa (third-party remake), Deathmatch and Codename: Gordon stay as spin-offs. Dropped Counter-Strike (its own franchise), Uplink (demo), Lost Coast (tech demo), Guard Duty (fan game).

Infamous.notes: Festival of Blood and First Light are standalone expansions per Wikipedia and show as spin-offs. Second Son (2014-03-21) precedes First Light (2014-08-26).

Jak and Daxter.notes: Wikipedia lists six games without a main/spin-off split; all six kept. Jak X (racing) and Daxter (PSP, Ready at Dawn) are the most debatable.

Killzone.notes: Wikipedia says the series consists of six games, handhelds included. Shadow Fall - Intercept is a standalone expansion and stays a spin-off.

Kingdom Hearts.notes: 393742 is IGDB's original 2002 release; 1219 (588 ratings) is typed as its expanded game. Re:coded is listed without remake_of because its original (coded, 20285) is a mobile game. 0.2 counted as main as most players do; chi/Union chi, Dark Road and Melody of Memory left as spin-offs (Wikipedia does not classify them).

Kirby.notes: Main series follows Wikipedia's 'traditional platformers'. Kirby Super Star (3719) is typed as a bundle in IGDB. Return to Dream Land Deluxe (typed expanded game) is listed as a remake of Return to Dream Land. Dropped ids are the Super Star / Super Star Ultra sub-games that IGDB lists as separate games.

Mario.notes: Sections follow Wikipedia's List of video games featuring Mario. Super Mario Bros. 2 (1067) is typed as a port of Doki Doki Panic in IGDB. Yoshi's Island is kept in Super Mario because Wikipedia lists it there. Super Mario Run is mobile but in Wikipedia's Super Mario list. Compilations (All-Stars, 3D All-Stars), Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and 3D World + Bowser's Fury are left out as re-releases; Super Mario Maker for 3DS is a port. Mario Kart Tour and Dr. Mario World (mobile) omitted. Drops: Smash Bros. and Luigi's Mansion entries attached to Mario.

games.title: Mega Man 2
Mega Man Battle Network 6: Cybeast Falzar
Mega Man Battle Network 6: Cybeast Gregar

Mega Man.notes: Sub-series as on Wikipedia. Mega Man 2 uses the original 1988 Rockman 2 entry (170742); the English 1715 is typed as its expanded game. BN6 uses the original Rockman EXE 6 entries because IGDB types the English ones as expanded games. Game Boy titles (Dr. Wily's Revenge, II to V) sit in the classic timeline as Wikipedia does.

Metal Gear.notes: Includes Metal Gear (1987) and Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, which IGDB attaches only to its 'Metal Gear' franchise, along with The Twin Snakes, Acid, Acid 2, Survive and Snake's Revenge. Rising, Ghost Babel and Portable Ops are spin-offs per Wikipedia. Dropped: Document of MGS2 and Digital Graphic Novel (not games).

Metroid.notes: 342602 is IGDB's original 1986 Famicom Disk release; 1101 (242 ratings) is typed as its expanded game. Prime Hunters, Pinball and Federation Force are spin-offs. Metroid Prime Remastered is a remaster and is not listed. Dropped: Smash Bros. games.

Monster Hunter.notes: Wikipedia's main series includes the G/Ultimate releases and the Portable/Freedom versions; IGDB types most of them as expanded games, so their ids are used. Iceborne and Sunbreak are expansions (type 2) that Wikipedia lists with the main series; remove them if the timeline should hold only standalone games. Stories, Frontier, Online and mobile titles are spin-offs. Dropped: Digimon Color Monster Hunter (Digimon product).

Mortal Kombat.notes: Twelve fighting games as listed by Wikipedia. Mythologies, Special Forces and Shaolin Monks are spin-offs. Ultimate MK3 and Trilogy are update releases and not listed separately. Dropped: Giga Fighters handheld toy and Puzzle Kombat (a minigame inside Deception).

Need for Speed.notes: Matches Wikipedia's main table, including Shift, Shift 2, Nitro, World and the mobile No Limits. Hot Pursuit Remastered is a remaster. Dropped: Most Wanted demo and Edge (cancelled beta).

Ninja Gaiden.notes: Wikipedia main line: NES trilogy plus the numbered 3D games. IGDB types the 1988 NES game (210484) as a port of the arcade game (7558), so the NES id is used. Shadow, Dragon Sword, Yaiba and Ragebound are spin-offs per Wikipedia; Black, Sigma, Sigma 2, Razor's Edge and Ninja Gaiden II Black are enhanced versions, not separate entries.

Persona.notes: Persona 2 entries (11453, 11454) are only under IGDB's Megami Tensei franchise. Persona 5 Strikers is a spin-off per Wikipedia. FES, Portable, Golden and Royal are enhanced versions. Persona 4 Revival (Feb 2027) is unreleased. Dropped 263596 (Digital Collection, a compilation).

Pokémon.notes: Core series per Wikipedia, including the enhanced third versions (Yellow, Crystal, Emerald, Platinum, Ultra Sun/Moon), which IGDB types as expanded games. Japanese Green has no separate IGDB entry; Red (1561) and Blue (1511) carry 1996. Colosseum, XD, Mystery Dungeon, Ranger, Conquest, Battle Revolution, the TCG game, Champions and Pokopia are spin-offs. Winds and Waves (2027) unreleased.

Prince of Persia.notes: Prince of Persia 3D is the third main game. Classic (2007) is Wikipedia's 'enhanced remake' of the 1989 game. The Rogue Prince of Persia (2025) is not labelled by Wikipedia; kept as a spin-off since it is a roguelike by another studio (ambiguous). Battles and The Fallen King are spin-offs. The Sands of Time remake was cancelled in 2026.

Professor Layton.notes: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright is a crossover (spin-off). Layton Brothers: Mystery Room is a mobile spin-off with no IGDB entry in the cache. New World of Steam (Dec 2026) and the Curious Village remake are unreleased. Katrielle is labelled spin-off in one Wikipedia table but the main series in its text; kept as main.

Ratchet & Clank.notes: Size Matters, Secret Agent Clank, All 4 One and Full Frontal Assault are spin-offs per Wikipedia. Quest for Booty and Into the Nexus are mainline. PlayStation Move Heroes is a crossover.

Rayman.notes: Rayman Legends uses 193359 (the original 2013 game); IGDB holds most ratings on 1968, which it types as a port. Raving Rabbids and Hoodlums' Revenge are spin-offs. Rayman Legends Retold is not released.

Resident Evil.notes: Numbered games plus Code: Veronica and Zero (not numbered, but most players count them as main). Revelations 1 and 2, Operation Raccoon City and Resident Evil 4 VR (172560, a VR version, not a remake) are spin-offs. Dropped 90566 (Beginning Hour, a teaser demo). Resident Evil Veronica remake (2027) unreleased.

Silent Hill.notes: Wikipedia main series: 1, 2, 3, 4, Origins, Homecoming, Downpour; Shattered Memories is a re-imagining of the first game; Silent Hill 2 (2024) is a remake. Wikipedia explicitly calls Silent Hill f a spin-off and Townfall a standalone spin-off, so both are left out of main even though Konami marketed f as a new mainline entry (debatable). P.T. is a playable teaser, left as a spin-off.

Sonic The Hedgehog.notes: Wikipedia's list does not label a main series explicitly; this follows its platformer tables and the usual main-series reading. Spinball, Sonic R, Sonic Battle, Chronicles and Sonic Boom are spin-offs. Sonic X Shadow Generations (2024) only exists in IGDB as a bundle (284716); the standalone Shadow Generations (320861) stays a spin-off to avoid a duplicate. 19538 is the 1996 Game Gear Sonic Blast (not 198604).

Spongebob Squarepants.notes: Wikipedia has no 'main series' for SpongeBob; it lists SpongeBob titles separately from Nicktoons crossovers. Main here = the retail console/PC/handheld SpongeBob games in that first table; small PC, mobile and edutainment titles and the Nicktoons crossovers (including Globs of Doom) are left as spin-offs. Judgment call, chosen for the app's purpose.

Star Fox.notes: Star Fox 2 listed at its 2017 release. Star Fox Adventures counted as main per Wikipedia. Star Fox Guard left as spin-off. 234945 is an undated duplicate 'Star Fox' entry.

Tales of.notes: Mothership titles per Wikipedia. IGDB 1202 'Tales of Destiny II' is Tales of Eternia (its NA name); 1203 is the separate 2002 Tales of Destiny 2. Tales of Hearts exists in IGDB only as its two paired DS editions, both listed. Tempest and Legendia are listed as mothership per Wikipedia although later reclassified by Bandai Namco. Dawn of the New World is an escort title (spin-off). Phantasia Full Voice Edition (PSP) treated as a port, not listed.

The Legend of Zelda.notes: Oracle of Seasons/Ages are a pair (two ids). Four Swords uses the standalone 163572 entry (shipped with A Link to the Past on GBA). The Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake (405460) releases 2026-11-05, so it is not listed yet.

The Sims.notes: Wikipedia main series is the four numbered games; MySims, Medieval, Castaway, Urbz, Bustin' Out, Stories, Online are spin-offs. 228496 is a console version of The Sims 3: Pets typed as standalone expansion.

Tomb Raider.notes: Legacy of Atlantis (2027) and Catalyst (2028) are unreleased. 130808 is the level editor tool.

Uncharted.notes: Wikipedia lists The Lost Legacy and Golden Abyss as spin-offs; many players count The Lost Legacy as main, but Wikipedia is explicit so it stays a spin-off.

Wario.notes: Wikipedia splits Wario Land, WarioWare and other games. Mega Party Game$! (GameCube) is typed as a remake of Mega Microgame$! in IGDB. Game & Wario is listed by Wikipedia within WarioWare as a spiritual successor. Mario & Wario, Wario's Woods, Master of Disguise and Bird & Beans stay as spin-offs. The WarioWare games have IGDB main franchise Mario, so they must be force-included by id.

Wars.notes: Single chronological list (Wikipedia does not formally split it). Re-Boot Camp is typed as a bundle in IGDB and remakes both Advance Wars 1 and 2; remake_of points to the first. Game Boy Wars Turbo is an enhanced version, not listed. Battalion Wars 1 and 2 are spin-offs.

Wolfenstein.notes: Wikipedia's Wolfenstein article could not be fetched (allowlist); list is from its games table as known plus common player consensus. Wolfenstein 3D uses 284 (typed as bundle, 311 ratings); 262516 is a low-rated duplicate. Enemy Territory (free multiplayer-only), Wolfenstein RPG (mobile) and Cyberpilot (VR) left as spin-offs. Spear of Destiny (standalone prequel) counted as main.

X-COM.notes: XCOM: Enemy Unknown (2012) is a reboot/re-imagining, listed as its own entry rather than a remake. Wikipedia includes Interceptor among the core 1990s games but also calls it a spin-off; most players count it as a spin-off, so it is not listed. The Bureau is a spin-off. 143076 is a duplicate entry of the Enemy Within expansion.

Yakuza: Like a Dragon.notes: Per Wikipedia, Like a Dragon Gaiden and Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii are spin-offs (some players count Gaiden as mainline). Like a Dragon: Ishin! remakes a spin-off, so it is not main. Dropped: Infinite Wealth trial version and two free-to-play app versions of Ishin! and 0.

spin.title: Age of Empires: The Age of Kings (DS)

Age of Empires.notes: Wikipedia counts the four numbered games as main; Age of Mythology (and its Retold remake) is called a spin-off. Definitive Editions are remasters, not listed as main.

Alien.notes: Film license umbrella (Wikipedia: List of Alien, Predator, and Alien vs. Predator games): unrelated tie-ins and standalone games by many developers, no main game series.

Anno.notes: IGDB names Anno 1404 by its North American title 'Dawn of Discovery'. DS/Wii games and Anno Online are spin-offs.

Danganronpa.notes: Wikipedia calls Ultra Despair Girls and Unlimited Battle spin-offs; main series is the numbered trilogy. Danganronpa 2x2 (2027) not yet released.

Divinity.notes: Wikipedia calls Dragon Commander a spin-off. Beyond Divinity kept as main (core RPG line). Fallen Heroes was cancelled; new 'Divinity' unreleased.

F.E.A.R..notes: Extraction Point and Perseus Mandate are expansions; Combat and Online are multiplayer spin-offs.

Ghosts 'n Goblins.notes: Follows Wikipedia's Arthur games list, which includes the remixes Chōmakaimura R (GBA, IGDB has it only as an expanded edition of Super Ghouls 'n Ghosts) and Gokumakaimura Kai. Gargoyle's Quest/Demon's Crest and Maximo are spin-offs. Ghosts 'n Goblins 64 was cancelled.

Golden Sun.notes: Wikipedia lists only the three main games, no spin-offs. 356272 is an undated N64 'Golden Sun' entry (unreleased prototype), dropped.

main.name: Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life

Harvest Moon / Story of Seasons.notes: Main series per Wikipedia's Story of Seasons list (Bokujo Monogatari, released in the West as Harvest Moon until 2014). Wikipedia also lists the variant releases For Girl, More Friends of Mineral Town, Another Wonderful Life and DS Cute as main entries, so they are included. Bokujou Monogatari: Shiawase no Uta (JP 2005) is the original of Magical Melody, titled with the Western name; IGDB 3386 (Magical Melody) is its expanded version. Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life (2023) is not in the cache, given by name. Spin-offs per Wikipedia (Innocent Life, Puzzle de Harvest Moon, My Little Shop, Frantic Farming, Hometown Story, PopoloCrois, Doraemon games, Rune Factory) and Natsume's own later Harvest Moon series (Lost Valley, Skytree Village, Light of Hope, One World, Winds of Anthos, Echoes of Teradea...) are left as spin-offs via IGDB. Harvest Moon: Boy & Girl (PSP compilation) and Tale of Two Towns+ (3DS port) not listed as main.

Horizon.notes: Wikipedia: Zero Dawn and Forbidden West are the main installments; Call of the Mountain (VR) and LEGO Horizon Adventures are spin-offs (already attached by IGDB). Zero Dawn Remastered is a remaster, not listed as main. Steel Frontiers and Hunters Gathering are unreleased.

Jurassic Park.notes: Movie tie-in umbrella: Wikipedia's 'Jurassic Park video games' article describes a collection of licensed games by many developers per film, with no main series. Only Jurassic World Evolution (Frontier) forms a coherent sub-series.

LittleBigPlanet.notes: Wikipedia says the series 'comprises six games' without naming them; its timeline also has Prehistoric Moves (called a spin-off), Karting, Run Sackboy! Run!, Sackboy: A Big Adventure and Ultimate Sackboy. Main here = the create/share platformers most players count (LBP, PSP, LBP2, PS Vita, LBP3); Karting and Sackboy: A Big Adventure are treated as spin-offs. 77349 'LittleBigPlanet HUB' was never released.

Mafia.notes: Wikipedia main series: Mafia, Mafia II, Mafia III, Mafia: The Old Country; Definitive Edition of Mafia is a full remake. Mafia II Mobile and Mafia III: Rivals are mobile spin-offs (attached by IGDB). Mafia II: Definitive Edition is a remaster, not listed.

Marvel's Spider-Man.notes: Wikipedia's lead calls Miles Morales 'a direct spin-off title' (also 'standalone'), so it stays in spin-offs although many players count it as a main entry. Marvel's Wolverine (2026) shares the Insomniac continuity but is not a Spider-Man game; left in spin-offs rather than main. Remastered is a remaster. Spider-Man 3 unreleased.

Mystery Dungeon.notes: Kept as a guide (not excluded): Wikipedia has a Mystery Dungeon series article and list, organised by sub-series (Dragon Quest/Torneko, Shiren, Chocobo, Pokemon, Etrian, other), and Shiren the Wanderer has no other franchise entry in the cache. Sections follow that list, Shiren first as Chunsoft's own line. Shiren includes numbered games 1-6 plus the GB, GB2 and Gaiden entries; DS/PC remakes linked with remake_of. Shiren Monsters: Netsal, Dragon Quest Mystery Dungeon mobile games, Nightmare of Druaga, Mystery Chronicle: One Way Heroics are not in the cache and are not listed. Chocobo's Mystery Dungeon Every Buddy! and Torneko Classic HD are remasters, listed as spin-offs. BS (Satellaview) episodes and Fuurai no Shiren Mega (mobile) left to the automatic rules.

Oddworld.notes: Wikipedia splits the Quintology (Abe's Oddysee, Munch's Oddysee) from bonus games (Abe's Exoddus, Stranger's Wrath); all four are counted as main here, as players do. New 'n' Tasty is a remake of Abe's Oddysee. Soulstorm is described as a reimagining of Abe's Exoddus and a sequel to New 'n' Tasty, so it is a main entry without remake_of. Game Boy/GBC/GBA handheld versions listed as spin-offs per Wikipedia. Undated IGDB entries (Squeek's Oddysee, Hand of Odd, Fangus Klot, Munch's Exoddus, SligStorm) are cancelled or unreleased.

Outlast.notes: Wikipedia: Outlast, Outlast 2, and The Outlast Trials (described as a prequel, multiplayer); kept Trials as main since it is the third full release. Whistleblower is DLC. Outlast 3 announced only.

S.T.A.L.K.E.R..notes: Four main games. 2025 Enhanced Editions are console/PC remasters of the trilogy, not listed as main. Dropped unreleased 'Untitled Expansion 2'.

main.title: Digital Devil Story: Megami Tensei (computer version)

Shin Megami Tensei.notes: Follows Wikipedia's main-series section of List of Megami Tensei video games, which starts with the two Digital Devil Story games (PC and Famicom versions are separate games) and includes Nine and Imagine (online MMO); most players count only the numbered games plus if..., Strange Journey and IV Apocalypse. Persona, Devil Summoner, Last Bible, Majin Tensei, Devil Children, Digital Devil Saga, Devil Survivor are spin-off series (all attached by IGDB). Dropped crossovers/hardware (BlazBlue Cross Tag Battle, PlayStation Classic, Smash DLC, costume DLC, Pillar of Amala) and the two 1995 SFC remake entries already covered by Kyuuyaku Megami Tensei.

Sly Cooper.notes: Dropped crossovers PlayStation Move Heroes and PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale. Bentley's Hackpack not in cache.

Sniper Elite.notes: Wikipedia main entries: Sniper Elite, V2, III, 4, 5, Resistance. Nazi Zombie Army and VR games are spin-offs. Zombie Army follow-ups not in cache. V2 Remastered left out of main (Wikipedia does not list it separately).

Star Wars Battlefront.notes: Main: 2004, 2005, 2015, 2017. Renegade/Elite Squadron (PSP/DS) and Mobile Squadrons are spin-offs. Classic Collection (2024 bundle) listed as spin. Dropped cancelled Battlefront III, companion app, and Battlefront+ mod entry.

Tetris.notes: Tetris has ~220 versions, so 'main' = the official versions Wikipedia's Tetris article names as notable, plus Puyo Puyo Tetris 2 (not named by Wikipedia but a major release). Tetris Forever is only a bundle on IGDB. Skipped the BPS Famicom and EA mobile versions (IGDB splits them per platform). Dropped multicarts/compilations and the Minecraft DLC pack.

The Dark Pictures Anthology.notes: Directive 8020 (May 2026) is listed by Wikipedia as a main entry (season branding dropped). Switchback VR is the spin-off.

The Elder Scrolls.notes: Wikipedia's main series is the five numbered games (Arena through Skyrim); Online, Battlespire, Redguard, Travels, Legends, Blades, Castles are spin-offs. Oblivion Remastered (2025, full UE5 rebuild) included as remake of Oblivion; Skyrim Special/Anniversary Editions not. Dropped unreleased TES VI, cancelled Travels: Oblivion, pinball tables, Minecraft mash-up and a Fallout bundle.

The Last of Us.notes: Two main games plus the Part I remake. Left Behind is standalone DLC (stays in spin-offs). Remastered versions are not separate entries. The Last of Us Online was cancelled.

sections.name: Trails from Zero / Trails to Azure (Crossbell)

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero
The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure
The Legend of Heroes II: Prophecy of the Moonlight Witch
The Legend of Heroes: A Tear of Vermillion
The Legend of Heroes III: Song of the Ocean

The Legend of Heroes.notes: Wikipedia's list groups games as Dragon Slayer, Gagharv trilogy and Trails (Liberl, Crossbell, Erebonia arcs, Reverie, Calvard arc). Trails sections listed first as most important. Gagharv entries use the Japanese PC-98 originals with English titles; the PSP versions (the English releases) are listed as remakes. Zero/Ao no Kiseki use the 2010/2011 originals; the 2020 English 'Trails from Zero/to Azure' Kai releases and all Evolution versions are enhanced ports, left out of main. Trails Beyond the Horizon placed with the Calvard arc. Nayuta and Ys vs. Trails in the Sky are spin-offs. Vantage Master Portable is a different Falcom series.

The Walking Dead.notes: Main = the four Telltale seasons. 400 Days is DLC of Season One; Michonne is Telltale's mini-series spin-off (IGDB parent game not in cache, given by name). Other licensed games (Survival Instinct, Overkill's, Saints & Sinners, Destinies etc.) are spin-offs. Dropped: crossover DLC in other games (Tekken 7, Dead by Daylight, World War Z, Funko Fusion) and pinball table DLC.

Total War.notes: Main = Wikipedia's main-entry table (historical and Warhammer). Saga titles (Thrones of Britannia, Troy), Fall of the Samurai (standalone expansion), Spartan: Total Warrior, Total War Battles and Arena stay as spin-offs. Medieval III and Warhammer 40,000 are announced, unreleased. Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed dropped (crossover).

Until Dawn.notes: Only one main game so far plus the 2024 remake. Rush of Blood (non-canonical VR spin-off) and The Inpatient (VR prequel) are spin-offs. Until Dawn 2 is due 2027.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War.notes: Three released main games. Winter Assault, Dark Crusade, Soulstorm, Chaos Rising and Retribution are expansions (spin-offs view). Dawn of War IV was delayed to December 2026 (IGDB 2026-12-03), not yet released, so not listed. Wikipedia series article could not be fetched directly; checked via the Dawn of War IV article and search results.

Yoshi.notes: Main = the platformers Wikipedia names (Yoshi's Island line, Woolly World, Crafted World, Mysterious Book) plus Yoshi's Story, which Wikipedia groups with the puzzle-leaning games but most players count as a main platformer. Universal Gravitation/Topsy-Turvy, Touch & Go, Yoshi (1991), Yoshi's Cookie, Yoshi's Safari, Tetris Attack stay as spin-offs. Hello, Yoshi! (IGDB 2025) not mentioned by Wikipedia; left as spin-off. Dropped: Smash, Mario Kart, Mario sports/party, Nintendo Land, Game & Watch remakes, Mario Kart Tour events, cards, demo, SNES Classic and other games that belong to other franchises.

main.title: Ys V: Lost Kefin, Kingdom of Sand

Ys.notes: Main = Ys I to X plus Origin, with Falcom remakes Ys Eternal (Ys I), The Oath in Felghana (Ys III) and Memories of Celceta (Ys IV). Ys IV only existed as two licensed 1993 versions (Mask of the Sun, The Dawn of Ys); both listed, Celceta marked as remake of Mask of the Sun. Taito PS2 remakes (Ys IV A New Theory, Ys V Lost Kefin PS2), Ys 2 Special, compilations (Complete, Chronicles) and Memoire remasters left out of main. Ys X: Nordics was wrongly in spin-offs. Zwei is a separate Falcom series (dropped).
